topics.title: Regions & AZs
topics.description: A region is a geographic area; an availability zone is an isolated datacenter within it.
key_points: Run at least 2 AZs for production.
The load balancer spreads instances across AZs.
RDS multi-AZ means a synchronous standby with automatic failover.
Multi-region only when RTO and RPO demand it - it brings consistency complexity.

topics.title: IAM
topics.description: Identity and permissions in one paragraph, plus the sound bite interviewers are listening for.

principles.title: Least privilege
principles.description: Grant the minimum set of actions on the minimum set of resources.

principles.title: Roles, not keys
principles.description: Applications get roles - EC2 instance profile, EKS IRSA, pod identity - never hardcoded access keys.

principles.title: Policies
principles.description: JSON allow or deny statements over actions plus resources.

topics.sound_bite: No credentials in code or config - the workload assumes a role and the SDK picks it up from the environment.

topics.title: Messaging
topics.description: SQS vs SNS vs Kinesis/MSK, one of the most frequently asked cloud comparisons.

options.title: SQS
options.description: Queue with one consumer group semantics. The message is deleted after processing. Visibility timeout, and a DLQ after N failures.

options.title: SNS
options.description: Pub/sub broadcast that pushes to many targets: SQS queues, Lambda, email. The classic combo is SNS to multiple SQS queues for fan-out.

options.title: Kinesis / MSK (Kafka)
options.description: Ordered, replayable stream with multiple independent readers.

topics.title: Serverless Trade-offs
topics.description: Lambda has zero idle cost and scales instantly, but the constraints matter more than the pitch.

tradeoffs.title: Cold starts
tradeoffs.description: Painful on the JVM. Mitigations: SnapStart, provisioned concurrency, or a lighter runtime.

tradeoffs.title: Stateless
tradeoffs.description: No local state survives between invocations.

tradeoffs.title: Where it fits
tradeoffs.description: Good for glue code and event handlers, not for latency-sensitive core APIs. Say that judgment out loud.

topics.title: 12-Factor Checklist
topics.description: The cloud-readiness highlights that come up when an interviewer asks what makes an app cloud-ready.

factors.title: Config in the environment
factors.description: Not baked into the jar. Spring profiles plus environment overrides.

factors.title: Stateless processes
factors.description: Session and state live in Redis or the DB; any instance can die.

factors.title: Logs to stdout
factors.description: The platform ships them to CloudWatch or App Insights.

factors.title: Disposability
factors.description: Fast startup and graceful shutdown via server.shutdown=graceful.

factors.title: Dev/prod parity
factors.description: The same image everywhere; Testcontainers locally.

topics.title: Interview Questions
topics.description: The five cloud questions a Java backend candidate should be able to answer cold.

questions.question: Your service on EC2 or EKS needs to read from S3. How do you give it access?
questions.description: An IAM role attached to the instance or pod (instance profile, IRSA), with a policy scoped to the bucket and the actions. The SDK resolves credentials automatically. Never access keys in environment variables.

questions.question: How would you make a single-region app highly available?
questions.description: Multi-AZ first: load balancer across AZs, RDS multi-AZ, Redis with replicas. Multi-region only if RTO and RPO demand it - route with weighted or failover DNS, replicate data with Aurora Global or Cosmos multi-region, and accept the consistency complexity.

questions.question: How do you handle secrets in the cloud?
questions.description: Secrets Manager or Key Vault, injected at runtime as a property source or mounted volume, with rotation enabled. IAM or RBAC controls who reads them, and CloudTrail or Azure Monitor provides the audit trail.

questions.question: Lambda vs a container service for a REST API?
questions.description: Spiky or low traffic with simple handlers points to Lambda, where idle cost is near zero. Steady traffic, JVM warmup and a complex framework point to containers. Mention cold starts and SnapStart for Java.

questions.question: What changes in your Spring Boot app when moving to the cloud?
questions.description: Ideally only configuration: externalized config, stateless sessions, stdout logging, health probes exposed, object storage instead of local disk, and queue-backed async work. If code must change, the app was not 12-factor.
